title: Efficient approximation of vessel wall stress under pulsatile hemodynamics using a snapshot-based coupling framework
authors: Se Hyeog Kim, Wonjin Choi, Hyeok Sul Kwon, Chanhee An, Hyun Jin Kim
affiliation: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), Daejeon, South Korea
used_for: ch2 Method 1 — the cost-effective (snapshot-based) FSI framework itself; cited as the tool that powers stage-1 dataset generation
verbatim_quote: The proposed method combines a one-dimensional (1D) reduced-order hemodynamic model with steady 3D fluid and structural analyses. First, pulsatile pressure and flow-rate waveforms are computed using a physics-based 1D reduced-order model. Boundary conditions are then extracted at representative time instants and applied to steady 3D fluid simulations to reconstruct wall traction. Finally, the transferred traction is used in a steady structural analysis to estimate the corresponding vessel-wall stress.
verification_status: verified — quote read directly from the source PDF (authors' own manuscript)
